nodes.name: Ti3C2 MXene etching
nodes.procedure: The Ti3C2 MXene was synthesized by etching 1.0 g of Ti3AlC2 powder in a mixture solution of LiF (1.32 g) and hydrochloric acid (6 M, 20 mL) for 24 h at 35°C. After several centrifugation-rinsing cycles with deionized (DI) water, the products were dispersed in 500 mL of DI water and kept under ultrasonic for 3 h. The dark green supernatant was collected by centrifugation at 2000 rpm for 1 h and was stored at 4°C in N2-filled bottles before use.

nodes.name: MXene/NF assembly
nodes.procedure: Typically, a piece of Ni foam (NF, 1×3 cm²) pre-treated with 2.0 M HCl was immersed into an aqueous suspension of Ti3C2 MXene (3 mg mL⁻¹) for 30 min. Then the MXene/NF was dried in vacuum at 60°C for 12 h.

nodes.name: NiFe-LDH electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: The NiFe-LDH/MXene/NF was made by the electrodeposition method. The MXene/NF was used as the working electrode. A Pt foil and an Ag/AgCl electrode with saturated KCl solution were employed as the counter and reference electrode, respectively. The typical potentiostatic deposition of NiFe-LDHs was carried out at -1.0 V for 300 s at room temperature on a CHI 760D potentiostat–galvanostat. The electrolyte is a mixed aqueous solution of 12 M Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and Fe(NO3)3·9H2O with a molar ratio of 1:1. Various NiFe-LDH/MXene/NF electrodes were also fabricated by tuning the deposition potential (-0.8 to -1.2 V), time (60-360 s) and the molar ratio between Ni and Fe salts (1:3 to 4:0). As comparison, the NiFe-LDH/NF was also produced by similar way except to use pristine NF as the working electrode.
nodes.source_text: 2.3. Synthesis of NiFe-LDH/MXene/NF The NiFe-LDH/MXene/NF was made by the electrodeposition method... The sample with the highest OER and HER activity is obtained at a deposition potential of -1.0 V for 300 s with a Ni²⁺:Fe³⁺ ratio of 1:1 in the precursor solution.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM reveals uniform coverage of MXene layer around macroporous NF scaffold and dense network of amorphous NiFe-LDH nanosheets (100-130 nm thick) with mesopores on MXene surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) examination reveals the uniform coverage of MXene layer around the scaffold of macroporous NF via plane-to-plane stacking of MXene sheets ... dense network of amorphous NiFe-LDH nanosheets with very thin thickness of approximately 100–130 nm and mesopores of tens nanometers between them on MXene surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows amorphous texture of NiFe-LDH nanosheets with very thin thickness and mesopores between them.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analysis at higher magnification indicates the even growth of dense network of amorphous NiFe-LDH nanosheets ... TEM image revealing the amorphous texture of NiFe-LDH nanosheets with very thin thickness.

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping shows uniform distribution of Fe, Ni, Ti, O and C elements in NiFe-LDH/MXene/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The presence and uniform distribution of Fe, Ni, Ti, O and C elements in NiFe-LDH/MXene/NF is visualized by elemental mapping analysis.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows only two sharp peaks at 44.9° and 52.3° from NF substrate; no NiFe-LDH peaks due to amorphous nature.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray powder diffraction (XRD) analysis of NiFe-LDH/MXene/NF exhibits only two sharp diffraction peaks at 44.9° and 52.3° from the NF ... No diffraction peaks of NiFe-LDH nanosheets are recorded since they are amorphous in nature.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey confirms presence of Fe, Ni, Ti, O, C in NiFe-LDH/MXene. Ti 2p deconvoluted into Ti-C (455.1/460.8 eV), Ti²⁺ (456/461.7 eV), Ti³⁺ (458.1/463.8 eV), Ti-O (458.7/464.4 eV). Ni 2p (Ni²⁺) at 855.8/873.5 eV shifted +0.5-0.6 eV higher vs pristine NiFe-LDH. Fe 2p (Fe³⁺) at 713.6/725.7 eV also shifted higher. Ti 2p peaks shifted -0.53 eV vs pristine MXene indicating charge transfer from NiFe-LDH to MXene.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) survey scan confirms the co-existence of Fe, Ni, Ti, O and C elements in NiFe-LDH/MXene peeled off from the NF ... The Ti 2p spectrum from Ti₃C₂ MXene can be deconvoluted into four pairs of 2p₃/₂/2p₁/₂ doublets including Ti–C (455.1/460.8 eV), Ti²⁺ (456/461.7 eV), Ti³⁺ (458.1/463.8 eV,) and Ti–O (458.7/464.4 eV) ... The Ni 2p spectrum shows two characteristic peaks at 855.8 and 873.5 eV ... The Fe 2p spectrum features with two prominent peaks at 713.6 and 725.7 eV ... Compared to pristine NiFe-LDHs, the Ni 2p and Fe 2p peaks from NiFe-LDH/MXene are apparently shifted by 0.5-0.6 eV to higher binding energy. While the Ti 2p peaks are negatively shifted by 0.53 eV with respect to pristine MXene.

nodes.characterization_summary: Contact angle of NiFe-LDH/MXene/NF is 57° (hydrophilic) vs 116° for NiFe-LDH/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After the growth of NiFe-LDH nanosheets, the NiFe-LDH/MXene/NF still possess good hydrophilic characteristics with a much smaller CA of 57° with respect to NiFe-LDH/NF (116°).

nodes.characterization_summary: EQCM shows water adsorption capacity of 0.12 g/g for NiFe-LDH/MXene vs 0.04 g/g for NiFe-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance (EQCM) analysis further identify the much higher capacity of water adsorbed on NiFe-LDH/MXene/NF (0.12 g g⁻¹) than that of NiFe-LDH/NF (0.04 g g⁻¹).

nodes.evidence_snippet: The FTIR-ATR spectrum recorded after water adsorption shows an obvious band at 1631 cm⁻¹, corresponding to the bending vibrations of O–H bonds of adsorbed water molecules. It is red-shifted by 6 cm⁻¹ compared with the band of NiFe-LDH/NF (1637 cm⁻¹).
